title: Tool‑Augmented Post‑Processing of Identical LLM Candidates for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration (shared_initial_candidate evaluation)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1) that isolates the effect of deterministic post‑processing (a NetOps verifier + lightweight topology simulator) on deterministic‑validator pass/fail outcomes when the same single LLM candidate is reused verbatim across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Planned: 300 paired tasks (600 episodes); completed: 598 episodes → 299 complete pairs. For the 299 analyzable pairs the archived contingency is n11=299, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; both baseline and guarded arms accepted the identical candidates (299/299). Paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10k resamples, seed=1729). All raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, task manifests, and execution logs are archived with SHA‑256 hashes (see Disclosure). Under the shared_initial_candidate semantics this run shows no downstream‑postprocessing effect on the deterministic validator verdict for identical candidates; it does not answer whether independent tool‑augmented generation would change generation quality or safety.

sections.introduction: LLM‑assisted intent→configuration pipelines are being explored to reduce operator burden in NetOps. Typical architectural patterns pair a generative model with deterministic validators/simulators and optionally repair loops. These generate–validate–repair chains aim to improve operational correctness, but empirical evaluations often conflate (A) improvements in generation quality and (B) the effect of downstream tool‑assisted post‑processing. The present study isolates (B) by fixing generation: a single LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate) was produced per task and reused verbatim by both the baseline and the guarded pipelines. The primary research question (preregistered) is: does applying a deterministic verifier and topology‑aware post‑processing to an identical LLM candidate change the deterministic‑validator pass/fail outcome? Our contribution is a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment with complete provenance and analysis artifacts, reporting the exact observed contingency and its statistical assessment.
sections.related_work: Prior work spans intent‑driven network configuration (intent→config) using LLMs, generate–validate–repair architectures, and verifier‑augmented agents. Representative verified sources that motivated aspects of our design include: intent→configuration translation (Nguyen et al., 2024, doi:10.1002/nem.2313), pretrained configuration models (PreConfig, arXiv:2403.09369), domain tool design and RAG agent prototypes (preprints such as 10.20944/preprints202604.1820.v1), and reliability/validator discussions in tool‑augmented agent literature (e.g., WeClaw‑style runtime work and verifier tradeoffs, 10.2139/ssrn.7317098; domain tooling for firewall config, 10.5220/0013221900003890). Those works justify evaluating verifier roles and motivate strict preregistration with artifact hashing.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1 before execution (SHA‑256: 991674d51794b41cf66471509149237b9a99f709b69aa3408d3d9d2ea2d50fc0). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on a deterministic‑validator pass indicator. Design semantics (frozen): shared_initial_candidate — for each task a single LLM generation was produced and reused verbatim by both pipelines (documented per‑episode provider trace and shared response file; see Reproducibility). Sampling and power. Planned n=300 paired tasks with strata: 150 simple, 150 complex. Power analysis (pre‑lock) targeted detecting a 0.20 absolute paired difference assuming baseline≈0.60, α=0.05, power=0.90. Execution contract and model. Adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; artifact SHA‑256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Generation budget: one shared generation per task; maximum model_calls pre‑registered = 600 (one per task + repair allowances). Verifier and simulator. Deterministic validator used: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0). Validator semantics: parses candidate commands to a canonical configuration, enforces per‑task workflow constraints (e.g., make_before_break, shutdown_configure_restore), computes final_state snapshots in a lightweight topology simulator, and emits violation codes when constraints or invariants are breached. Preregistered exclusion and missingness rules. Exact‑string matches to a curated public config corpus were to be excluded from confirmatory analysis (moved to exploratory). Technical provider failures are logged; primary analysis uses complete pairs (pairs with both outcomes present). Sensitivity analyses treating failed runs as verifier‑fail were pre‑registered. Execution logging, hashing, and provenance. All raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces and scoring JSONs, task manifests, and the execution log were archived and SHA‑256 hashed (execution/*). Primary artifact pointers and authoritative hash manifest are recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json (see Disclosure). Statistical analysis. Primary test: exact McNemar two‑sided on paired binary outcomes; supplementary bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for the paired difference. Secondary descriptive cost metrics: model‑call counts and wall‑clock latencies (Wilcoxon signed‑rank where applicable). All analysis executors and parameters were frozen and are archived (analysis/*).
sections.results: Execution and analyzable sample. Planned episodes: 600 (300 pairs). Completed episodes: 598. Failed episodes: 2 (forming a single missing pair, pair‑000269); complete analyzable pairs = 299. Model‑call accounting: model_calls_used = 300 (execution manifest). Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact‑backed). The verified paired contingency table for the 299 analyzable pairs (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 d77df43abf83e081bb5a3c3a21fa0de67afd72628ee5ed880f2bff810e627174) is: n11 = 299, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline success rate = 299/299 (100.0%); guarded success rate = 299/299 (100.0%). Estimated paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (artifact: analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg). Representative scored episodes and validator traces. Per‑episode scoring JSONs include normalized_response, raw_response_sha256, validator_trace with final_state, parsed_command_count, required_command_count and difficulty metadata (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore). Example artifacts: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (sha256: 8f38c8becd7e1e36...), execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256: 6569b491...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha256: cefa6344...). Missingness post‑mortem. The single excluded pair (pair‑000269) corresponds to two failed episodes arising from a failed shared_initial provider call; the provider call failure event and the provider trace are archived (execution/provider_calls/task-000269-shared-initial.json) and the execution log records the event (execution/execution_log.jsonl; SHA‑256 b45a600859502b088a9416744ccbff3f5fba2e6dd76b863440bdfd36ebf21bb8). Per our preregistered missingness plan the pair was excluded from the primary complete‑pair analysis; all failure artifacts are preserved for audit. Ceiling effect note. The observed baseline success rate (1.00) deviates from the preregistration assumption (≈0.60), producing a ceiling effect that makes the originally targeted minimally important effect (+0.20) unobservable in this execution. We therefore report exact counts, the exact McNemar p‑value, and the degenerate bootstrap CI rather than interpreting the run as a powered null result.
sections.discussion: What this run does and does not show. The run answers a narrowly stated, preregistered estimand: when the same single LLM candidate is reused verbatim (shared_initial_candidate) by both pipelines, deterministic verifier + simulator post‑processing did not change the deterministic validator pass/fail outcome in our confirmatory set (299/299 concordant acceptances). Importantly, this does not imply verifier tooling is unnecessary: validators provide explicit violation codes, final_state snapshots, and audit trails (valuable for operations), and they are essential when generation quality is lower or when independent generation is used. Ceiling and design implications. The preregistered power calculation assumed a moderate baseline pass rate; the observed ceiling eliminated the ability to detect the targeted effect. Future experiments intended to measure downstream tooling impact on operational outcomes should (A) adopt independent per‑condition generation semantics (not shared candidate reuse), (B) use harder or adversarial task strata to avoid ceiling effects, and (C) replicate across multiple model families and seeds. Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial semantics intentionally eliminate generator variance but also preclude evaluating tool‑influenced generation improvements; provider call failures were handled per preregistered rules and logged (one excluded pair; artifacts archived). Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes a curated rule set (workflow patterns and invariants); it is a proxy for operational correctness but cannot capture all hardware/vendor idiosyncrasies. External validity: tasks used deterministic synthetic topologies and vendor‑agnostic CLI fragments; generalization to production vendor CLIs, telemetry conditions, or wider task classes requires replication. Conclusion validity: the ceiling effect constrains interpretability of null change; reported exact counts and archived artifacts provide a reproducible factual record.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired run that held generation constant (shared_initial_candidate), deterministic verifier+simulator post‑processing did not change deterministic validator pass/fail outcomes: both arms accepted the identical candidates in all 299 analyzable pairs (n11=299). The result is narrowly scoped to the preregistered estimand and does not address whether independent agentic, tool‑augmented generation would yield different or safer candidates. We provide complete provenance: raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, task manifests, analysis artifacts, and full SHA‑256 manifests to enable independent audit and reproducibility. We outline concrete design recommendations for follow‑up studies that evaluate tool‑augmented generation rather than post‑processing alone.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory Disclosure Statement: This manuscript and all reported results derive from an autonomous post‑lock research run governed by the immutable initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The experiment was preregistered as cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1 and frozen prior to execution (preregistration SHA‑256: 991674d51794b41cf66471509149237b9a99f709b69aa3408d3d9d2ea2d50fc0). Declared LLM used: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; artifact SHA‑256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Orchestration/adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0). Generation semantics required by the preregistration and executed here: shared_initial_candidate — for each paired task a single LLM candidate was produced and reused verbatim by both the baseline and guarded pipelines. The shared candidate raw response files are archived at execution/responses/task-<NNN>-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256s recorded under execution/*) and the provider call traces for these shared generation events are archived at execution/provider_calls/task-<NNN>-shared-initial.json (see execution manifest for the full per‑file hash list). Execution accounting: planned episodes = 600 (300 pairs); completed episodes = 598; failed episodes = 2 (forming one missing pair, pair‑000269); analyzable complete pairs = 299. The failed shared_initial provider call that produced the missing pair is recorded in the execution log (execution/execution_log.jsonl; SHA‑256: b45a600859502b088a9416744ccbff3f5fba2e6dd76b863440bdfd36ebf21bb8) and in the corresponding provider trace execution/provider_calls/task-000269-shared-initial.json. All raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, task manifests, analysis artifacts, and a full manifest of SHA‑256 artifact hashes are archived and serve as the authoritative source for every reported number (authoritative manifest path: execution/execution_manifest.json; see execution manifest for per‑file hashes). No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock; all manuscript numeric claims are grounded in these archived execution and analysis artifacts. This run followed the preregistered analysis plan (paired exact McNemar and bootstrap CI) and the missingness/contamination rules; any deviations are recorded in the execution/analysis manifests. The present manuscript reports only the narrowly preregistered estimand (effect of downstream tooling on identical LLM candidates) and explicitly does not claim results about independent tool‑augmented generation without further experiments.
limitations: The executed semantics fix generation by reusing a single shared LLM candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate); results therefore answer only whether post‑generation tooling changes deterministic validator pass/fail for identical candidates, not whether independent tool‑augmented generation would produce different or safer outputs.
Tasks used deterministic synthetic topology templates and a lightweight simulator; external validity to vendor‑specific CLIs, device‑level idiosyncrasies, or production telemetry is limited.
Only one declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) was used; results do not generalize across model families or scales without replication.

The deterministic validator enforces a curated rule set and workflow constraints; it cannot exhaustively model every hardware or vendor behavior and thus is an imperfect proxy for full production correctness.
A ceiling effect occurred: observed baseline success = 299/299, invalidating the preregistered power assumption and preventing detection of the originally targeted minimally important effect.
